quizName: Computing Systems, Hardware, Software, and Data

questionVariants: What makes up a computing system?
What two kinds of parts work together in a computing system?
How would you describe a computing system to a classmate?
What does the term computing system mean?
What must work as a team to form a computing system?
answerVariants: Physical equipment and programs that work together to handle information.
Machines and the instructions they run, acting as a team to work with data.
A team of equipment and programs used to handle information.
Physical parts joined with programs to do work with data.
Equipment working with a set of instructions to handle information.

concepts.conceptName: Four Main Jobs of a Computing System
questionVariants: What are the four main information jobs of a computer?
Which four jobs make up the basic model of how a computer works?
What four kinds of work does the basic computer model include?
Which four jobs should a diagram of a basic computer system include?
What are the four main jobs used to explain how a computer handles information?
answerVariants: Input, processing, storage, and output.
Receiving data, working on it, keeping it, and giving results.
Taking data in, following steps to use it, saving it, and producing results.
Getting data, acting on it, saving it for later, and giving a result.
Input to receive data, processing to use it, storage to keep it, and output to give results.

concepts.conceptName: How Typed Information Moves Through a Computer
questionVariants: Trace what happens inside a computer when you type your name, see it, and save it.
How do the parts of a computer handle a word from the first key press until it is saved?
Explain the steps that let a typed message appear and be kept for later.
What steps connect typing a name, seeing it on a display, and saving the document?
Describe the path a typed word takes before you can see it and open it again later.
answerVariants: Input enters, instructions process it, working memory holds it, output presents it, and storage keeps it for later.
Data comes in, programs and equipment work on it, memory holds the current work, output presents it, and storage keeps a copy.
The system receives data, handles it using instructions and memory, produces visible output, and stores a copy for later use.
Incoming data is processed and held in memory, then presented as output and kept in lasting storage.
Input is processed with help from working memory, presented as output, and placed in storage for later use.

concepts.conceptName: Working Memory Compared With Saved Storage
questionVariants: How does working memory differ from storage for saved files?
Why do working memory and saved-file storage have different jobs?
Compare the jobs of working memory and long-term storage.
What is the difference between memory for current work and a drive for saved files?
How do memory and lasting storage help a computer in different ways?
answerVariants: Temporary space holds what is being used now; lasting space keeps information even after power is off.
A short-term workspace holds information in use, while a lasting place keeps files through shutdown.
The temporary workspace helps with the task in progress; the lasting place keeps a copy without power.
Information in use goes in a temporary workspace; information needed later is kept in a place that lasts through shutdown.
A temporary workspace serves the task in progress, while a lasting place keeps information after shutdown.

concepts.conceptName: Computers Do Not Need a Traditional Shape
questionVariants: Why can a device count as a computer without a keyboard or monitor?

Must all computers look like the ones in a classroom? Explain your answer.
What should you remember before deciding a small device cannot contain a computer?
answerVariants: These systems come in many forms and can be built inside other products.
There are many possible shapes, including systems hidden inside other products.
Such systems can have different forms and work from inside a larger product.
A system may be built into another product instead of standing on its own.
Some systems are parts of other products, so their outside appearance can vary.

questionVariants: What makes a computer general-purpose?

How would you explain the job of a general-purpose computer?
What can a general-purpose computer do by running different software?

answerVariants: It can run many kinds of programs to do many different tasks.
It handles a wide variety of tasks by using different programs.
It uses many kinds of programs for activities such as writing and drawing.
It can do many tasks rather than being made for just one special job.
It runs a variety of programs, allowing it to do many kinds of work.

questionVariants: What makes a computing system embedded?
How is an embedded computer used in a product?
What does embedded mean when describing a computing system?
What job does an embedded computer have within a machine?
How would you describe an embedded computing system?
answerVariants: It is built inside another product to carry out a particular job.
It works as part of a larger device to do a specific task.
It is a built-in part of another product that helps that product do its job.
It is placed inside a larger device for a particular purpose.
It serves a specific task from inside another product.

questionVariants: What does hardware mean in computing?
Which parts of a computing system count as hardware?
How would you explain the word hardware?
What kind of thing belongs in the hardware category?
What makes something hardware in a computing system?
answerVariants: The real, physical equipment, both inside a device and attached to it.
Physical parts such as chips, screens, and cables.
Equipment you could physically touch, including internal and connected parts.
The actual machinery and other physical parts used by the system.
Physical equipment, whether it is inside the main device or connected outside it.

questionVariants: What is a computer peripheral?
How does a peripheral help a computer?
What makes an added device a peripheral?
What role does a peripheral have in a computer setup?
How would you describe a peripheral to someone setting up a computer?
answerVariants: An extra piece of equipment attached to add or extend an ability.
An added piece of equipment that connects to expand what the main machine can do.
An attached device that adds a useful function, such as printing or recording.
Extra equipment connected to give the main machine another ability.
An added device that extends the main machine's functions through a connection.

questionVariants: What does software mean in computing?
What kind of thing belongs in the software category?
How would you explain computer software?
What makes something software rather than a physical part?
What role does software play in a computing system?
answerVariants: Programs and instructions that tell equipment what to do.
The directions a machine runs to carry out its actions.
Programs that guide the actions of physical equipment.
Sets of instructions that direct what the machine does.
Programs, such as browsers and games, that give equipment its instructions.

concepts.conceptName: Different Software Gives the Same Hardware Different Jobs
questionVariants: Why can one laptop switch from drawing to doing sums without replacing any parts?
How can a Chromebook edit a picture and then open a website using the same equipment?
What lets a classroom machine change from writing a story to playing a game?
Why does switching activities on a laptop usually not require a new machine?
What allows a single device to carry out many activities while its physical parts stay the same?
answerVariants: Running different software gives the hardware a new set of instructions.
Different programs direct the hardware to do different jobs.
Changing the software changes the instructions that the hardware follows.
The hardware can follow a new set of directions when another program runs.
Programs supply different instructions, letting the hardware take on a new job.

questionVariants: What does data mean in computing?
How would you describe computer data?
What kinds of things count as data for a computing system?
What is meant by the word data when talking about computers?
What must something be like to count as computer data?
answerVariants: Information in a form a machine can use, keep, or send.
Information represented so it can be stored and worked on by a machine.
Machine-readable information, such as text, pictures, sounds, or numbers.
Information put into a form that equipment can store or work with.
Information represented in a way that programs and equipment can use.

answerVariants: 0 and 1.
Zero and one.
Only 0s and 1s.
Zeros and ones.

concepts.conceptName: A Photograph File Is Data, Not Editing Software
questionVariants: How do a saved photograph and the program used to change it differ?

answerVariants: The content being worked on is data; the tool that gives directions for changing it is software.

Stored content is data; the instructions that act on that content are software.

answerVariants: The physical part collects sound, and the instructions guide how the system handles it.
